newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends steady after early dollar demand.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends steady after early dollar demand.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended at 35.720/730 per dollar on Friday, almost unchanged from the opening level of 35.730/7350, dealers said.
The day was marked by good demand for cash dollars from large state-run companies. Their buying pushed the rupee down to 35.76 level, the lowest level the rupee touched on Friday.
Dealers said state-run firms in the market on Friday included the Steel Authority of India Ltd, National Thermal Power Corp Ltd and Oil and Natural Gas Corp Ltd.
"Around 1.30 p.m. the cash counter closed," said a dealer. "Thereafter there was hardly any demand," he said.

The withdrawal of the state-run firms and inward dollar remittances received by some foreign banks in Bombay helped revive the rupee, enabling it to spring back to the day's opening level, dealers said.
After two day's of aggressive dollar buying, the Reserve Bank of India abstained from the market on Friday, dealers said.
The forward dollar market did not see much action or volumes on Friday, dealers said. The six month annualised premium closed at 8.45 percent compared to Thursday's closing of 8.40 percent.
